subject: English
central_question: How can a student choose determiners and articles that express the intended quantity, definiteness, negation, and general meaning accurately?
in_scope_units: Positive and negative quantity with a few/few and a little/little
Use of the with superlatives, ordinal numbers, and unique nouns
Equivalent negative patterns with no and not any
Zero article with general plural and abstract or uncountable nouns

known_pitfalls.claim: Few and a few have the same meaning.
known_pitfalls.correction: A few has a positive sense meaning some, while few has a negative sense meaning almost none or not enough.

known_pitfalls.claim: Little can be used with plural countable nouns such as friends.
known_pitfalls.correction: Use few/a few with plural countable nouns and little/a little with uncountable nouns.

known_pitfalls.claim: Abstract nouns always require the article the.
known_pitfalls.correction: General abstract nouns often take the zero article, as in 'Honesty is important.'

recommended_example_progression: Choose between a few and few from intended meaning
Choose between a little and little with an uncountable noun
Insert the before a superlative, ordinal, or unique noun
Transform no into not any without changing meaning
Remove an unnecessary article before a general abstract noun
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Typical CBSE practice includes gap filling, omission, editing, and sentence rewriting with suitable determiners.
